versions.author: deepseek/deepseek-v3.2
versions.label: negative intensifier after 'so'
versions.trigger_hypothesis: The neuron fires negatively when the token is an adjective or adverb that follows the word 'so' and intensifies it, describing an extreme degree.
versions.output_hypothesis: The neuron's negative activation suppresses the generation of extreme intensifiers after 'so', perhaps to avoid hyperbolic or overly emotional language.
alternatives: The neuron detects the word 'so' followed by any adjective/adverb, regardless of meaning.
The neuron responds to any token that is a scalar adjective (like 'great', 'deep') in any context.
versions.adapter_changes: State B+1 consistently amplifies the negative activation (makes it more negative) across strong windows, especially in emotional_chat contexts (W22, W23, W24). State A+1 and C+1 slightly reduce the negative magnitude. State D+1 has minimal effect.
proposed_tests: 'so' + adjective vs. same adjective without 'so' :: [negative] The view was so beautiful. | [low] The view was beautiful.
'so' + adjective vs. 'very' + adjective :: [negative] It was so difficult. | [low] It was very difficult.
'so' + adverb vs. 'so' + noun :: [negative] He ran so quickly. | [low] He ate so soup.
'so' + extreme adjective vs. 'so' + neutral adjective :: [negative] The pain was so unbearable. | [low] The color was so blue.
'so' in emotional vs. factual context :: [negative] I miss you so much. | [low] The ratio is so 2:1.
'so' followed by adjective at sentence end vs. middle :: [negative] It is so cold outside. | [negative] It is so cold that I shivered.
'so' + adjective with positive vs. negative sentiment :: [negative] That is so wonderful! | [negative] That is so terrible.
'so' + adjective vs. 'such' + adjective :: [negative] She is so kind. | [low] She is such kind.
'so' + adjective in quoted speech vs. narrative :: [negative] He said, 'This is so easy.' | [negative] The process was so easy.
'so' + adjective after comma vs. directly after 'so' :: [negative] It was, so beautiful, to see. | [negative] It was so beautiful to see.

versions.author: claude-opus-5-5 (review)
versions.label: 'so + adjective' degree slot (negative); n_amp+1 adds negative shift on exclamatory assistant replies
versions.trigger_hypothesis: Base negative: the adjective/adverb completing a degree 'so X' (also 'such a X', weaker 'very/too X'), independent of meaning or sentiment; conventional 'so sorry' is exempt. Base positive (partial): copula/auxiliary after a sentence-initial pronoun ('It's', 'I'm', 'We've been').
versions.output_hypothesis: Negative activation lowers further intensifiers (pretty, quite, really) and 'That', raises plain continuations ('it', 'you'); positive raises evaluative openers ('Great', 'How'). Weak at natural size (KL about 0.2 at the reply start).
alternatives: Negative branch tracks exclamatory/emphatic register in general, with so+adjective its main carrier (explains e19, base -5.8 on 'Oh' after good news).
n_amp+1 change is a context-wide offset on any reply the model classifies as emotional (argued against by the factual-reply control).
versions.adapter_changes: n_amp+1: new strong negative response on reply-initial interjections and emotive reply text (e.g. 'Oh' +0.2 -> -16.3), valence-independent, absent for factual replies; little extra on the base trigger. n_sup+1: shrinks the negative branch, mostly inside assistant replies ('so nervous' -9.4 -> -0.9 in a reply vs -13.1 -> -11.0 in plain text). o_amp+1 like n_amp+1 at about 1/3-1/2 size; ctrl+1 near base.
proposed_tests: Zero L26/N8828 in n_amp+1 on the 20 behavior prompts; count so+adjective and '!' per reply vs a layer-matched random neuron.
Sweep fixed phrases 'so sorry / so grateful / so glad / so happy' to map the exemption.
Patch L26/N8828 to base values at reply-initial tokens in n_amp+1 and measure next-token change.
